questions.question: Which language should the worksheet builder use?
questions.rationale: The stated preference is HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and no existing framework is present.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for larger frontend codebases.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Plain browser JavaScript, matching the requested beginner-friendly HTML/CSS/JS approach.

questions.question: Which frontend framework or approach should be used?
questions.rationale: The user prefers HTML/CSS/JS and requested a project suitable for a beginner on Windows.

options.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
options.description: A straightforward browser app with no framework setup.

questions.question: What should the frontend include?
questions.answer: Responsive form for subject, grade, topic, difficulty, question types, language, answer key, and instructions; worksheet preview and PDF download.
questions.rationale: These are the core user-facing requirements supplied for the project.
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive form for subject, grade, topic, difficulty, question types, language, answer key, and instructions; worksheet preview and PDF download.

questions.question: Which language should the worksheet API use?
questions.rationale: Python with Flask was the recommended stack in the prior project discussion.

options.label: Python
options.description: Pairs with Flask and is approachable for a beginner.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses the JavaScript runtime for the API.

questions.question: Which backend framework should be used?
questions.rationale: Flask was preferred in the prior discussion for a beginner-friendly Windows project.

options.label: Flask
options.description: A small Python web framework with a simple learning curve.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: A typed Python API framework with automatic API documentation.

questions.question: What should the backend include?
questions.answer: Validate worksheet inputs, call a real AI provider using a server-side secret, return structured questions, and support Unicode-capable PDF export. Include focused tests and beginner-friendly PowerShell setup instructions.
questions.rationale: This captures the required generation, security, PDF, testing, and Windows setup behavior.
questions.recommendedChoice: Validate worksheet inputs, call a real AI provider using a server-side secret, return structured questions, and support Unicode-capable PDF export. Include focused tests and beginner-friendly PowerShell setup instructions.

questions.question: Which real AI provider should generate worksheets? You can name one or leave it undecided for the plan to recommend.
questions.answer: Leave undecided; recommend a suitable provider in the plan.
questions.rationale: A real provider is required, but no provider or credentials were specified. Credentials will not be embedded in source code.
questions.recommendedChoice: Leave undecided; recommend a suitable provider in the plan.

questions.question: Which persistent data stores does the first version need?
questions.rationale: History and dashboards were optional; they are excluded from the smallest useful MVP.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Generate and download worksheets without storing user data or history.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Store worksheet history locally in a simple file-based database.

questions.question: Should users sign in to use the worksheet generator?
questions.rationale: Authentication was not part of the core requirements; user accounts, history, and dashboards were optional.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in for application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The first version is usable without accounts.
